evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs were exposed topically to Grillocyn HY 77, challenged after two weeks via duplicate closed patches, and scored at 2, 24, and 48 h after patch removal using the Draize scale (0-4) for erythema, eschar, and edema.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig sensitization test, Grillocyn HY 77 was applied via closed patches. At challenge, test and control animals were scored using the Draize method for erythema and edema. A score of 0 was reported for each test and control animal during each of the three grading periods, and Grillocyn HY 77 did not produce a positive reaction in any of the test animals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction and challenge phases in guinea pigs; very slight or well-defined skin reactions observed in induction; challenge: very slight erythema in 1 animal, well-defined erythema in another, slight edema in one.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig sensitization study, kojic acid was tested with an induction phase and a challenge phase. Very slight or well-defined skin reactions were observed in a few animals during induction. Following challenge, very slight erythema occurred in 1 animal and well-defined erythema in another at 24 and 48 hours, with slight edema in one animal at 48 hours. The authors concluded that kojic acid should not be classified as sensitizing to the skin.
